findings.text: follow-on: the evidence fragment (and the manifest, echoed in the commit body) states 'All 328 changed float fields moved at the last-bit level only -- max relative change 2.3e-13 on physical quantities', but 2.3e-13 is the max over the headline aggregate scalars only (ledger.common_sol). Over the full changed population of physical quantities (|value|>1) the max relative change is 1.619e-10, at per_cell[111].current_a (1.7545606765386679 -> 1.7545606762546715). The conclusion that the drift is numerical rather than physical is unaffected and independently confirmed here, but the stated bound does not cover the per-cell fields the sentence claims to bound. Recommend restating the figure as the headline-scalar bound (2.3e-13) separate from the per-cell bound (1.6e-10), both numerical.

item_verdicts.float_drift_is_numerical: PASS in conclusion, with a corrected figure. The receipt's floats changed, and every change is numerical noise, not physical: the changed set is 314 per_cell float leaves plus the top-level scalars and the render sub-receipt's mirrors. Over the headline aggregate quantities the max relative change is indeed 2.3e-13 (ledger.common_sol 1072.7057484194079 -> 1072.7057484191655, rel 2.3e-13) and 3.1e-14 (ledger.core / plasma_current_a, rel 3.2e-14); both are the last few ulps of a float64. Over the FULL changed population the max relative change on a quantity of magnitude > 1 is 1.619e-10, at per_cell[111].current_a (1.7545606765386679 -> 1.7545606762546715); the four leaves with relative change above 1e-6 are all values of order 1e-13 or smaller where the relative measure is meaningless (see naive_0.50_field). A 1.6e-10 relative drift in a per-cell ampere value across 1248 commits of equilibrium/solver change is floating-point reduction drift, not a physical change, and it sits far below the printed two-decimal precision the verdict and title use. The conclusion holds; the manifest's blanket 'max 2.3e-13' applies to the headline scalars only and does not bound the per-cell fields.
item_verdicts.goal: PASS. Independently confirmed by direct extraction from both commits: old receipt (a6fe0d05b) has key support_clip_mode = {available:false, reason:'...'}; new receipt (c65d9832) has key clip_mode = 'chord' and no support_clip_mode. The retired key is gone.
item_verdicts.naive_0_50_field: NAMED AND EXPLAINED. The 'naive 0.50' figure in the manifest is topology_branch.axis[1]: 1.0176606877547874e-13 -> 2.049496285730968e-13, rel 5.035e-01 (mirrored exactly at render.nulls.axis[1]). It is NOT a physical change: both values are of order 1e-13, i.e. essentially zero, so the relative measure has no physical meaning -- a quantity indistinguishable from zero changed by another quantity indistinguishable from zero. The same holds for the other three large-relative leaves: fixed_point_residual 1.57e-14 -> 2.72e-14 (rel 0.42, the solver residual at its machine floor) and render.nulls.strike_points[0][1] 3.53e-13 -> 6.90e-13 (rel 0.49, a near-zero coordinate). topology_branch.axis[0] (1.0138, rel 9.2e-15) and boundary_flux (1.5406, rel 1.9e-14) confirm the genuine, non-zero quantities drift only at the last few ulps.

justifications.durability: The reviewed commit has a conventional bodied message with no AI attribution, is the reviewed worktree HEAD, the worktree is clean, and the evidence fragment and gate logs are committed/durable alongside it.
justifications.evidence: The record rests on the run's readable head gate (test module 4 passed), an independently reproduced reader guard with a firing negative control, an independent base re-run of the same test module (4 passed), and a full structural and float-level comparison of both committed receipts. The one deduction is a quantitative overstatement in the manifest and evidence fragment: the blanket 'all 328 changed float fields moved at the last-bit level only, max relative 2.3e-13' is true only for the headline aggregate scalars, whereas the full changed population drifts up to 1.619e-10 relative (per_cell[111].current_a). The corrected figure does not change the conclusion -- both are floating-point reduction drift across 1248 solver commits, far below the printed two-decimal precision -- but the stated bound does not cover the per-cell fields it claims to bound, so the evidence dimension is scored 17 rather than higher.
justifications.fit: The change reuses the existing fit: the committed driver benchmarks/sol_ledger_current_census.py is re-run with its committed arguments and the committed reader/guard is left to do its job, rather than authoring new machinery or hand-editing the receipt. Re-running the driver (rather than patching the JSON key) is what makes the receipt reproducible and keeps the figure and render receipt consistent with it.
justifications.goal_fidelity: The node's goal is met exactly: the committed receipt now carries clip_mode='chord' and no support_clip_mode, and the consumer benchmarks/net_current_scaling_census._read_sol_ledger reads it without raising (independently reproduced, with the retired-key receipt raising ValueError as the negative control). Verdict, cell counts and all categorical fields are identical between the two receipts.
justifications.scope_discipline: The commit touches exactly the five paths inside the declared write scope and nothing else: no product source, no test, no plan file, no shared index.
